authority: This file is the single source of truth for authentication/security test requirements shared by CI and live staging testing.
maintenanceRules: Change a requirement here first; CI mappings and live pass/fail criteria must not be edited independently.
Any auth/security defect must map to an existing case or add a new LIVE-AUTH case, with CI regression coverage where technically possible and live coverage where deployment/provider behavior matters.
A live case with CI coverage=gap must state why repository CI cannot or does not yet cover it.
Invitation controls remain explicitly not-applicable until a real invitation feature is introduced.

cases.title: Email/password signup succeeds and establishes the correct initial account state

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
steps: Create a fresh Pixelsmith E2E mailbox.
Complete signup with valid required fields and a valid password.
Complete any real email verification/OTP step delivered to the mailbox.
Observe the post-signup destination and persisted account state.
pass: Exactly one account is created for the normalized email identity.
The verification/OTP is accepted only once and the user lands in the expected onboarding/account state.
fail: Signup creates duplicate identities, skips required verification, leaks sensitive data, or lands in an unauthorized state.
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Session fixation, token tampering, stale-session replay, and revoked-session reuse fail closed

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use only disposable test identities and test data.
steps: Capture pre-login and post-login session state.
Verify session rotation/authority transition.
Attempt safe replay of stale/revoked/tampered session material only on disposable accounts.

For protected page routing, explicitly verify /dashboard, /admin, and /onboarding (plus representative descendants where applicable) redirect an unauthenticated or server-invalid session to /sign-in; separately verify a genuinely authenticated non-admin user still receives the configured authorization-denial behavior for /admin.

With an authenticated protected dashboard already open, invalidate that session server-side, then return focus to the browser without clicking a dashboard control or refreshing; verify the stale protected page immediately leaves for /sign-in.
pass: Authentication does not preserve attacker-controlled pre-auth authority; stale/revoked/tampered sessions are rejected by protected resources with a clean redirect/denial (307 to /sign-in for unauthenticated /dashboard, /admin, and /onboarding page access; null/401/403 for an API). An already-open protected page whose session later becomes invalid automatically leaves for /sign-in when the browser resumes/focuses and identity revalidation returns null, without requiring a click or manual refresh. An authenticated but non-admin account may still receive the deliberate branded 404 for /admin. An uncaught server error or a 404 caused solely by an expired/missing session is a failure.
fail: A stale, revoked, or tampered session grants authenticated authority, OR its rejection surfaces as an uncaught error/generic error boundary rather than a clean redirect/denial, OR an already-open protected page remains visible after session-loss revalidation (for example, only swapping to logged-out navigation until the user clicks or refreshes).
cleanup: Remove disposable state only after evidence is captured; preserve failed-flow state when needed for debugging.
evidence: Record URL, role, action, HTTP status, relevant screenshot/trace, and any console/network error. Never record secrets.

cases.title: Ordinary member sessions use a 7-day idle timeout and 14-day absolute lifetime while privileged sessions retain strict limits

preconditions: Use the designated staged/live hostname, never a Vercel preview or localhost.
Use disposable ordinary-member and Administrator/Super Admin test identities.
steps: Authenticate as an ordinary member and verify the issued session remains valid beyond the former 30-minute idle and 12-hour absolute windows, using controlled test-time/session evidence rather than waiting in real time.
Verify the ordinary-member policy is 7 days idle and 14 days absolute, with activity refreshing only the idle timestamp and never the absolute deadline.
Authenticate as an Administrator or Super Admin and verify the privileged session still uses the existing 30-minute idle and 12-hour absolute policy.
Verify the Active sessions UI/listing applies the same role-specific idle policy and does not hide a still-valid ordinary-member session or retain an idle-expired privileged session.
pass: Ordinary-member sessions use a 7-day idle limit and fixed 14-day absolute limit; privileged sessions remain 30-minute idle and fixed 12-hour absolute.
Role-specific active-session listing matches token validity and activity never extends the absolute deadline.
fail: An ordinary member is still forced out by the old 30-minute/12-hour policy, a privileged account receives the longer member lifetime, or active-session listing disagrees with actual token validity.
cleanup: Sign out disposable sessions and remove any temporary privileged role/test state after evidence is captured.
evidence: Record role, issued/observed expiry policy, relevant session-list behavior, HTTP status, and any screenshot/trace needed to prove the deployed behavior. Never record cookie/token values.
